current_research_question: For a residential property in a named Costa Blanca town, what does each published price series actually measure (asking, registered sale, appraisal), at what geography and reference period is each published, and which of them — if any — is evidence of what a buyer would pay for that specific home?
must_establish: Separate four instruments and never merge them: (1) portal asking-price data, which is private and advertised, not paid; (2) the Catastro's valor de referencia, an administrative value; (3) transaction and deed evidence from the Colegio de Registradores and the Consejo General del Notariado, which is what buyers actually paid; and (4) MIVAU valor tasado, which is an APPRAISAL series and is never a record of what anyone paid.

Establish, for the specific town the piece names, whether any of these instruments publishes a figure at municipal level at all, and if not, name the smallest geography for which a figure exists and say so in the copy.

Determine, for each figure taken from a press release, whether 'Alicante' in that release means the city or the province, and confirm it against the publisher's own page rather than a search summary or aggregator.
Establish whether figures from different instruments may legitimately be compared or subtracted from one another, and if they may not, state the reason in the piece.
never_assume: That a province-wide figure describes any particular town, or that a town figure can be inferred from the province one.
That 'Alicante' in a portal press release means the province — it commonly means the city, which is not a coastal-resort market.
That asking price, registered sale price and appraisal value are versions of one number, or that the difference between two of them measures anything.
That municipal-level official data exists for smaller Costa Blanca towns — some publishers only disaggregate above a population threshold, so check before naming a town.
production_hook: Your Costa Blanca home can be described by several different price instruments: portal asking prices; the Catastro's valor de referencia; actual transaction and deed evidence from the Notariado and the Registradores; INE's price index at autonomous-community level; and MIVAU appraisal values. They measure different things and must never be treated as versions of one number.

current_research_question: Where a Costa Blanca home has built area on the ground that does not appear in the Registro de la Propiedad or the Catastro, what effect does that have on a mortgage valuation, on the buyer's finance and on the notarial deed — and what routes exist to regularise it before a sale?
must_establish: Establish what a declaración de obra nueva terminada requires under art. 28.1 of the consolidated Texto Refundido de la Ley de Suelo y Rehabilitación Urbana (RDLeg 7/2015) — certificación de técnico competente acreditativa de la finalización conforme al proyecto, proof of the requisitos de la legislación de la edificación for handover, and the administrative authorisations (or the acreditación that a comunicación previa / declaración responsable was filed and its period ran) — and separately what the obra nueva por antigüedad route requires under art. 28.4 TRLSRU, together with the grounds on which a Registrador must refuse it: an anotación preventiva for a live expediente de disciplina urbanística, suelo de carácter demanial, or suelo affected by servidumbres de uso público general. There is no single 'planning text': the state gateway is art. 28 TRLSRU, and the Valencian layer that fixes the 15-year restoration-of-legality clock is the TRLOTUP (Decreto Legislativo 1/2021), not Andalusia's AFO.
Establish whether and on what basis a mortgage valuer may include square metres that appear on neither the register nor the Catastro — do not infer this from what agents say.

Establish whether an unregistered extension prevents the notary from authorising the deed, or only affects price, finance and the buyer's own risk; if the answer is not established from a primary source, say in the copy that it is not.

Establish who initiates and pays for regularisation in the relevant municipality and what documentation the town hall requires, or state plainly that this varies by municipality and must be checked locally.
never_assume: That an undeclared extension makes the sale illegal or impossible — legality of the works, registrability of the title and saleability are three different questions.
That the antigüedad route is available for every property; land classification and public-use servitudes can exclude it, and a planning-discipline entry on the register can block it.
That Catastro area matching the deed means the works were lawfully authorised, or that a Catastro entry regularises anything.
That there is a known percentage a buyer knocks off for unregistered metres — no measured figure for the Costa Blanca has been established, so do not publish one.
production_hook: The pool, the glazed terrace, the extra bedroom: if the register has never heard of them, find out what they do to your price before the buyer's valuer does

current_research_question: Does an officially published administrative reference value apply to residential property in Alicante province in 2026, what instrument created it, which tax bases and which party's taxes does it govern, how is it updated and consulted, and does it have any legal effect on the price a seller and buyer may freely agree?
must_establish: Establish from a primary source (BOE / Catastro / Agencia Tributaria) whether a published reference value currently applies to residential property in the Comunitat Valenciana, and name the instrument and the year of the figure in force.
Establish precisely which taxes it forms the base for and which party pays those taxes on a sale — do not attribute it to the seller's taxes without checking.
Establish whether it has any binding effect on the freely agreed sale price, or only on a tax computation, and state that distinction explicitly in the copy.
Establish how an owner consults the value for their own property and what challenge or appeal route exists, if any, and how often the value is revised.
never_assume: That the reference value and the valor catastral are the same number or serve the same purpose — this is the distinction the piece exists to prevent collapsing.
That it caps, floors or otherwise determines what a buyer may pay, or that a sale below it is invalid.
That a figure published for an earlier year still stands — establish the update cycle and the year of the figure quoted.
That whatever it governs falls on the seller; establish which party's tax base it enters before implying anyone's bill changes.
production_hook: An administrative value may already be attached to your property — one you never commissioned and will not find on your deed. Find out whether yours has one, what it governs, and what it does not.

current_research_question: Over the most recent directly comparable periods, how have registered transaction counts and reported price levels moved in Alicante province, from which instruments, and what — if anything — can an individual owner conclude from that combination about the likely price and time to sell their own home?
must_establish: Establish the latest provincial transaction counts for Alicante from the national statistics instrument for periods that are genuinely comparable (same months, same series), and record the extraction date and that the series is subject to revision.

Establish which published time-on-market figures exist, exactly what event they time (advertisement live, offer accepted, deed signed), at what geography, and whether any exists below national or city level.
Before using any circulating average days-on-market figure, verify it against the named publisher's own release; establish whether that publisher publishes a mean at all, or only a distribution.
OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — only if the agency supplies it: their own first-asking to agreed-price gap and elapsed time, with the sale count and period stated. The post must stand up without it.
never_assume: That a listing removed from a portal was a sale — withdrawals, expiries, agent switches and re-listings all end an advertisement without one.
That a national or city-level time-on-market distribution describes the province or any Costa Blanca town.

That the widely repeated 'average 80-90 days' has a source; traced, it ends at agency blogs, not at the release it is attributed to. Where a publisher gives only a share distribution, treat it as a distribution - a skewed distribution does not disprove a long mean, and neither may be turned into the other.
That rising prices and a higher chance of selling move together, or that transaction counts and price levels measure the same thing.
production_hook: Price indicators and transaction volumes can move in opposite directions. What are Alicante province's latest readings right now, and what does each actually measure?

current_research_question: Which published instruments give a price per square metre covering this property's location, what event does each one actually measure, at what geography is each published, and for which period is the latest figure available?
must_establish: Establish which bodies publish a euro-per-square-metre figure that covers this property's location, and for each one establish what the underlying event is — an advertised asking price, a registered deed price, or a mortgage appraisal — and name it explicitly on the slide

Establish, for each instrument, the finest geography at which it is actually published, and whether a figure exists for this specific municipality at all or only for the province or the autonomous community
Establish the latest reference period each instrument has published as at the date of writing, and whether the periods being compared are the same
Establish, before any figure is used, that it was read from the publishing body's own release or table rather than from a news summary, a portal blog, or an AI answer that may have merged two numbers
never_assume: Never assume 'Alicante' in a portal press release means the province — in idealista's monthly releases it means the city, and the city is not a coastal resort market
Never assume the three instruments are versions of one number: they must never be subtracted from, averaged with, or corrected against one another

Never assume a province-wide figure describes a town, or that a town-level figure exists — official appraisal data is disaggregated only for larger municipalities, so several Costa Blanca towns have no official town-level price at all
Never reuse the province asking-price figure of 2,834 EUR/m2 that circulates in summaries — it is uncorroborated and may be a national number mislabelled
production_hook: Several sources and producers publish a price per square metre covering Alicante province — a ministry, the registrars, the notaries and the private portals — and they do not agree. Before you accept any valuation of your home, ask which one it was built on.

current_research_question: What published measures of time-to-sell cover this property's market, what event starts each clock and what event stops it, at what geography is each published, and what can end a listing without a sale having happened?
must_establish: Establish what the leading published time-on-market series actually measures — which event opens the clock, which event closes it, and whether closure of an advertisement is evidenced to be a completed sale
Establish whether that series is published as an average or as a distribution, and whether any average can legitimately be derived from what is published
Establish the finest geography for which any time-to-sell figure is published, and state plainly if no figure exists for this province or this town

Establish the provenance of any 'average days to sell in Spain' figure before quoting it — trace it to the publishing body's own release, and discard it if the trail ends at agency blogs repeating one another
never_assume: Never assume an advertisement coming down means a home was sold — withdrawal, expiry, a change of agent, and re-listing as a fresh advert all end a listing without a transaction

Never repeat the circulating '80-90 days average': traced, it ends at agency blogs repeating one another, not at any publishing body's release. Where a share distribution is published (sold under a week / under a month / over a year), use it as a distribution and never convert it into a single headline average - and note that a skewed distribution and a long mean are not in conflict, so do not treat one as disproving the other.
Never assume one property equals one listing clock — multi-agency listing is common here, so the same home can run several adverts with independent start dates
Never present a national or city-level distribution as if it described this town, and never convert a distribution into a single headline number
production_hook: Someone will tell you homes here sell in X days. Before you price to that number, ask what it counted — and whether anyone measures it for your town at all.

current_research_question: How have registered transaction counts and registered sale prices moved in this property's province, and in its municipality where published, over the most recent comparable periods — and which of the two tells a seller something about how many buyers are reachable for their home?
must_establish: Establish the registered transaction counts for this province for the most recent published periods and the equally-dated national counts, pulling both from the statistics office's own series and recording the extraction date, since these figures are provisional and get revised
Establish separately the registered sale-price series for the same province and periods, keeping it strictly apart from asking-price and appraisal series
Establish whether the transaction series can be split into second-hand and new-build for this province, since a headline provincial move may sit mostly in one of them

Establish whether a second instrument built on a genuinely different underlying source agrees on the direction of the volume move for this province and period, and say so if the two disagree. Note that INE's Estadística de Transmisiones de Derechos de la Propiedad and the Colegio de Registradores' Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria are both drawn from the Registros de la Propiedad, so they are not independent of one another and their agreement is not corroboration; an independent cross-check must come from notarial data (Consejo General del Notariado, Índice Único Informatizado / Portal Estadístico del Notariado).
never_assume: Never assume a price series and a volume series are the same story or that one explains the other — do not assert a cause for a divergence, only that both were measured
Never assume 'record prices' in a national or index-level release describes this province or this town, and never mix an index (trend only) with a euro level
Never assume a provincial volume move applies to a municipality, a price band, or a property type without a figure that is actually published at that level
Never turn a two-period move into a prediction about what prices or demand will do next

current_research_question: In this agency's own completed sales, what has been the relationship between the first asking price, any reductions made, and the final registered sale price — and how is a listing's age recorded when the same property is re-listed or marketed by more than one agent simultaneously?
must_establish: Establish, from the agency's own completed sales only, how first asking price related to final agreed price, over what period, across how many sales, and for which property types — and publish the sample size alongside any figure
Establish how portal listings record price changes and listing age, and whether removing and re-posting a property produces a new advert with a new date
Establish what happens in practice when the same property is advertised by several agents at once — whether prices and listing dates can differ across those adverts, and what a buyer sees

Establish which selling costs sit between the agreed price and what the owner actually receives, so that a reduction is discussed against the net rather than the headline, and check whether each of those costs is fixed, percentage-based, or negotiable
never_assume: Never use another agency's, a portal's, or a national reduction statistic as if it were this agency's own evidence — if the agency's book cannot support a number, publish no number

Never assume the agreed price is what the seller banks. Agency services carry VAT, but whether a quoted commission percentage already includes it is a fact of that agency's mandate — establish it, never assume either way. And where the seller is a non-resident, the buyer withholds 3% of the price as a payment on account: it is settled against the final liability, so it may be fully refunded, partly refunded, not refunded, or more tax may still be due. Never write that it is reclaimed later as though return were the default.

Never assume there is a legally set or capped agency commission rate in Spain, and never publish a 'typical Costa Blanca commission' figure as if it were measured — the published ranges are national and not an Alicante measurement
Never assume one property equals one advert with one price and one age, or that a re-listed property carries its previous history with it

current_research_question: When a property in Alicante province is sold by a seller who is not a Spanish tax resident, what withholding obligation arises, who is legally obliged to carry it out, what form and deadline apply to it, and by what procedure and timeline can the seller reclaim any amount withheld above the tax actually due?
must_establish: Establish which statute imposes the withholding on transfers by non-resident sellers, whether the obligation falls on the buyer or the seller, and whether it is characterised as a final tax or a payment on account

Establish which form the withholding is paid on, which form the seller uses to settle the actual liability, and the deadline running on each — and establish whether those deadlines are confirmed against a primary instrument or only secondary sources

Establish whether the withholding percentage is applied to the sale price or to the gain, and what happens when the tax actually due is lower than the amount withheld, or when the sale produced a loss
Establish whether the withholding rate or the mechanism changed in 2025 or 2026, and record whether 'no change located' is the same as 'no change exists'
never_assume: That the withheld percentage equals the tax owed — the two are computed on entirely different bases, and one may be larger or smaller than the other
That the seller controls the withholding — the obligation and the filing sit with the other side of the transaction, which is why a seller can be exposed by a counterparty's failure
That a refund is automatic — establish whether it requires an affirmative filing by the seller, and do not state a refund waiting time unless a source gives one

That 'non-resident' means 'foreigner' — tax residence turns on where a person actually lives, not on their passport, so a Spanish national living abroad and a foreign national living in Spain may fall on opposite sides of this rule
production_hook: Selling your Costa Blanca home while non-resident for Spanish tax purposes? The buyer must hand 3% of the price straight to Hacienda instead of to you — but it is a payment on account of your capital-gains tax, not the tax itself: once you file your modelo 210 you may get all of it back, some of it, or none, and you may still owe more. Here is who takes it, why, and how you settle it afterwards — whether any of it comes back depends on the gain.

current_research_question: For a residential sale in Alicante province, how is the taxable gain computed, and on what basis does the rate applied to that gain differ between a seller who is a Spanish tax resident and one who is not?
must_establish: Establish the statutory definition of acquisition value and of transmission value for a property gain, including which purchase-side costs may be added and which sale-side costs may be deducted, and which are expressly excluded
Establish the rate structure applied to a property gain for a Spanish tax resident, and separately the rate applied to a non-resident, and establish whether either is progressive or flat

Establish whether the non-resident rate on a property-transfer gain differs by the seller's country of residence, and separately establish whether any other IRNR rate that varies by country of residence applies to a different income type and is being confused with this one
Establish whether any rate or bracket applicable to property gains changed with effect from 2025 or 2026, and which instrument made the change
never_assume: That an EEA citizen and an EU citizen and a third-country national face different rates on this gain until it is established one way or the other — and never file a nationality under an immigration or tax category as shorthand
That the gain is sale price minus purchase price — establish the statutory computation before writing any worked example
That a rate that applies to one kind of non-resident income applies to a property gain; two different rates circulate and are routinely swapped
That every seller pays something — establish whether a loss, or a gain fully offset by allowable costs, changes the position
production_hook: Two sellers can face different capital-gains rate structures on identical sales because one is Spanish tax-resident and the other is not. Nationality alone does not decide it.

current_research_question: How is plusvalía municipal calculated on a residential sale in Alicante province, what choice if any does the taxpayer have between calculation methods, who is the taxpayer on an ordinary sale, and does that change when the seller is an individual living outside Spain?
must_establish: Establish the two calculation methods currently in force, which instrument rebuilt the tax after its predecessor was struck down, and whether the taxpayer may elect the method producing the lower base
Establish what happens where there was no increase in land value between acquisition and transmission — specifically whether that is a case of non-liability or of an exemption that must be claimed

Establish who is the taxpayer on an onerous transfer, and separately whether that liability shifts, and to whom, when the seller is a non-resident individual; establish whether a contractual clause between the parties binds the town hall

Establish the statutory ceilings that constrain plusvalía municipal (TRLRHL art. 107.4 for the coefficients, art. 108.1 for the rate, capped at 30%), confirm from the ordenanza fiscal of each specific municipality what that town hall has actually set, and treat any single quoted amount as a fact about one town only. Do not state a province-wide spread without having opened the ordinances it is drawn from.
never_assume: That a figure or rate from one Alicante-province municipality applies to any other — each town hall sets its own within legal maxima, so a number is a fact about one town, never about the coast
That there is always something to pay — establish the no-increase position before implying the tax is unavoidable
That the private contract decides who pays it; establish whether a clause between buyer and seller is effective against the town hall

That the shift of liability for a non-resident seller is a benefit to that seller — establish what it means in practice at completion, including whether the counterparty recovers the amount from the sale proceeds
production_hook: The town-hall tax on your sale can be worked out two ways, and if the real increase in the land's value is lower than the objective calculation you can ask for that lower figure to be used instead — plus one twist that only applies when the seller is an individual who is not resident in Spain.

current_research_question: Which exemptions can eliminate or reduce the tax on a gain from selling residential property in Spain, what conditions attach to each, and what determines whether a foreign owner of a Costa Blanca property can access them?
must_establish: Establish each exemption capable of reducing or eliminating tax on a residential property gain, the article behind it, and for each one whether it is open to residents only, to non-residents in certain states, or to both

Establish the precise condition each exemption attaches to the property itself — in particular whether it must have been the seller's habitual residence, and how that status is defined and over what period it is tested
Establish, for any exemption available to non-residents, exactly which states of residence qualify and what additional requirement the statute imposes on the state or on the use of the proceeds

Establish whether the practical conclusion — that a second home does not meet the habitual-residence condition — holds under current administrative practice, and flag it as open where the groundwork marks it unverified
never_assume: That an exemption available to a resident is available to a non-resident, or vice versa — establish each one separately and never generalise across the two

That a holiday home, a let property, or an inherited property that was never lived in by the seller meets a habitual-residence condition; establish how the condition is actually defined rather than inferring it

That an exemption open to residents of certain states is open on the basis of citizenship — establish whether the test is the seller's state of tax residence, and keep EEA, EU and third-country status distinct rather than merging them
That an age-based or reinvestment-based exemption has no conditions beyond the headline one — establish the reinvestment window, the proportion of proceeds required, and any time test on the property

current_research_question: Does a private homeowner who signs a marketing mandate with an estate agent in Spain have any right to withdraw from it afterwards, what determines whether that right exists and how long it lasts, and what — if anything — must an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana state in that document about their own registration?
must_establish: Establish from the consumer-protection code itself whether a withdrawal right attaches to service contracts of this kind, exactly what circumstances trigger it, how long the period runs, whether the length changes with the circumstances of signing, and what happens to the period if the agent never disclosed the right at all.
Establish whether a private individual selling their own home is a consumer for these purposes, and whether the burden of proving where a contract was concluded falls on the owner or on the agent.

Establish whether estate agency in the Comunitat Valenciana is subject to a register, whether entry is obligatory or voluntary, when that obligation began, what the agent must consequently include in the mandate, and whether a homeowner can verify an agent's entry themselves — and by what search route.

Establish whether exclusivity, penalty and post-termination commission clauses are governed by any statute at all or left entirely to contract, and what review, if any, applies when the client is a consumer.
never_assume: Do not assume a withdrawal right exists for every mandate — it is conditional, and the seed must publish the condition rather than the conclusion.
Do not assume any number of days; the period varies with the circumstances of signing and with what the agent disclosed, and more than one figure is in play.
Do not assume the profession is licensed, or that a regional register works the way another Spanish region's does; establish the current Valencian position and the date it took effect.
Do not assume a homeowner can look up one named agency directly — establish how the public search actually behaves before telling anyone to use it.
production_hook: The agency contract you signed at your own kitchen table may not bind you the same way as one signed in their office — check which one you have before you sign anything.

current_research_question: Which documents must a residential seller in the Comunitat Valenciana hold before completion, who bears the cost of each, and which of them genuinely prevents the deed from being authorised as opposed to merely exposing the seller to a penalty or to the buyer afterwards?
must_establish: Establish, from the state instrument that governs it, who must obtain the energy performance certificate on a sale, whether issue by a technician is sufficient or registration with the regional body is also required for legal validity, and how long a certificate lasts and on what that depends.

Establish whether the community-of-owners debt certificate is a bar on the notary authorising the deed, whether anyone can waive it and who, whether any deadline binds the person who must issue it, and what liability attaches to the property afterwards if it is skipped.

Separately establish that the habitability standard the declaration is measured against changed: Decreto 80/2023 (DC-23) was repealed by letra g of the disposición derogatoria única of Ley 5/2025, de 30 de mayo, and the Generalitat states that the Orden de 7 de diciembre de 2009 (DC-09) remains in force. Under the fichas annexed to Decreto 12/2021, DC-09 is the standard for buildings built or with a licence applied for from 7 April 2010 onwards, and HD-91 for everything before that, split into a pre-23 September 1989 existing-buildings ficha and a 23 September 1989 to 6 April 2010 new-build ficha.

Establish whether a missing energy certificate blocks the notary or only creates a sanction and buyer exposure; these two are routinely conflated and the answer must come from the instrument, not from a summary of it.
never_assume: Do not assume every missing document is a hard stop — decide for each one separately whether it blocks the signing, delays it, or only creates later liability.
Do not assume a certificate issued by a technician is a registered certificate; establish whether registration is a separate step and who must do it.
Do not assume any validity period, penalty amount or issuing deadline — several differ by rating, by severity and by region.
Do not assume the building-evaluation regime applies to the property in question; establish the age threshold and whether the rule is state, regional or municipal before applying it to anything.
production_hook: Some of the bills for selling arrive before a buyer does. The energy certificate, the occupancy paperwork, the community's debt letter — who pays each one, and which of them can actually stop the signing.

current_research_question: What does this agency charge to sell a home here, is that percentage quoted with or without the applicable tax, what work and which third-party costs does it include, and at what moment does it become payable?
must_establish: Obtain the agency's own fee structure in writing: the rate or scale, whether it is quoted inclusive or exclusive of the applicable indirect tax, and confirm the general rate of that tax for this service from the tax authority rather than from a blog.

Establish whether any published percentage band for Spain is a national market observation or a measured Costa Blanca figure, and label whatever is used as exactly what it is; if no local measurement exists, say that instead of implying one.
Establish whether commission rates are capped or regulated by any Spanish statute or set purely by contract, and where the agreed figure is required to be recorded.

Establish from the agency itself when the fee falls due — on a private contract, on completion at the notary, or otherwise — and what is owed if the sale collapses before completion, plus which costs (portal listings, photography, floor plans, translation) are inside the fee and which are billed separately.
never_assume: Do not assume a quoted percentage includes the indirect tax, and do not state that tax rate from memory.
Do not assume a Costa Blanca median commission exists — a nationally published band is not a local measurement and must never be presented as one.
Do not assume a multi-agency arrangement costs an owner the same as a sole mandate, or that agencies share one fee rather than each claiming their own.
Do not present this agency's own fee as typical of the area, or as high or low against neighbours, without evidence measured for the area.

current_research_question: On a residential sale in Alicante province, which amounts leave the seller permanently, which reduce the figure the seller is taxed on, and which are withheld at completion but later recoverable — and what does each of those outcomes depend on?
must_establish: Establish from the tax authority's own text which costs borne by the seller reduce the transmission value, and which costs borne at purchase raise the acquisition value — and what is explicitly excluded from each.

Establish the statutory default allocation of the deed, the first copy and the registry costs between seller and buyer, whether that default can be displaced by agreement, and which of the two actually governs in local practice on the Costa Blanca.

Establish who the taxpayer is for the municipal land-value tax on a sale, whether a different rule applies where the seller does not live in Spain, whether more than one calculation method exists and who chooses, and whether the bill varies between municipalities in the province.

Establish which items in the resulting list are permanent costs and which are payments on account that can be recovered, and what filing a seller must make, and by when, to recover anything recoverable.
never_assume: Do not assume local custom on notary and registry costs matches the statutory default — establish both, and say which one governs the contract being described.
Do not assume the municipal land-value tax is due at all, or that a figure from one town predicts another; the method and the rate are set locally.
Do not assume a sum withheld at completion is a cost — a payment on account, a tax finally due and an invoice are three different things and must never be added into one headline number.
Do not infer a seller's tax residence from their passport, and do not treat all non-resident sellers as a single category.
production_hook: The price on the listing is not the money that reaches your account. Some of what comes off is gone for good, some of it lowers the figure you are taxed on, and some of it — depending on where you are tax-resident — is only being held.

current_research_question: When a seller taxed as a non-resident completes a residential sale in Spain, what happens to the retained portion of the price — under whose legal obligation, through which filings, and on what deadlines — and what determines how much of it, if any, returns to the seller?
must_establish: Establish the statutory basis of the retention: whose obligation it is, what it is computed on (price versus gain), and its legal character as a payment on account rather than a final tax

Establish the filing instruments and deadlines on both sides of the retention, and from what date each period is counted — then check each deadline against a primary source rather than a repeated secondary one
Establish how the final liability on the gain is computed for a person taxed as a non-resident, and whether that computation differs from the one applied to a Spanish tax resident

Establish whether the rate applied to a property gain varies by the seller's country of tax residence — sources on this point conflict, so resolve it against the governing text before writing a single figure
never_assume: That the retained percentage equals the tax owed — it can exceed the liability, fall short of it, or be due back in full where there is a loss

That the property-gain rate varies by the seller's country: AEAT applies a flat 19% to a capital gain on a transfer for every non-resident. The 19%/24% split belongs to other non-resident income (imputed and rental), not to this gain — do not carry it across. Re-check the rate at generation time because tax law moves, but do not present it as contested.
That tax residence follows the passport, or that a foreign seller with a Spanish NIE, a padrón entry or a Spanish bank account is therefore a resident
That the refund arrives soon after the sale, or that any published turnaround time reflects what actually happens
production_hook: Sell as a Spanish non-resident and the buyer withholds 3% of the agreed price at completion. It is a payment on account, not the final tax: after Modelo 210, you may receive an excess refund, receive nothing back, or still owe more.

current_research_question: In computing the taxable gain on a Spanish residential sale, what may lawfully be added to the acquisition side and deducted from the transmission side, what documentary evidence does each item require, and what is expressly excluded?
must_establish: Establish which acquisition-side items the governing text admits — the price paid, the taxes and costs borne when buying, and spending on the property — and the exact wording that distinguishes an admissible item from an excluded one
Establish which selling-side costs the seller may deduct from the transmission value, and whether agency commission and the municipal land tax are among them
Establish how the acquisition value is fixed where the property was inherited or gifted rather than bought, and which document sets it
Establish what evidentiary standard applies — whether an invoice, a bank trace, or a registered work declaration is required — and what is excluded outright, financing costs included
