never_assume: Do not assume asking price is achieved price, or that a listing disappearing from a portal was a completed sale — withdrawals, expiries and re-listings all end an advert without a transaction.

Do not assume a national or province-wide figure describes Jávea, Torrevieja, Dénia or Alicante city; name the geography of every number used, and note that a release naming 'Alicante' may mean the municipality of Alicante/Alacant rather than the province — both are published under that name, by the INE and by the portals alike — so check which one it is before using the number.
Do not assume the widely repeated 'average days to sell' numbers are sourced — several circulating figures trace back to no published dataset and contradict the release they cite.

Do not assume that ending the tenancy in order to sell empty is available, quick or free; whether and how a landlord may end a live contract is a separate legal question that must be answered before the option is offered.

current_research_question: For a home in an Alicante-province coastal town, what published instruments (if any) measure how long a sale takes, what precise start and end event does each one use, and what share of listings end for a reason other than a completed sale?
must_establish: Establish, for each published time-on-market / 'días en venta' figure covering Spain or Alicante, the publisher's own definition: what event starts the measurement, what event ends it, and whether the output is a mean, a median or a distribution — quote the definition rather than the number.
Establish whether any time-on-market figure is published at Alicante province or municipality level; if none is, the piece must say so rather than substitute a national figure.
Establish what ends a listing other than a sale (withdrawal, expiry, change of agent, re-advertisement as a new ad) and whether any published series separates those outcomes from completed sales.
Establish whether one property marketed by several agencies generates several independent listing clocks, and how any published figure handles duplicate advertisements.
never_assume: That any circulating 'average days to sell' number — including the widely repeated 80–90 day figure — is sourced; check whether the publisher it is attributed to ever published a mean at all, and whether the sub-figures quoted alongside it match that publisher's own tables.
That a listing removed from a portal was a home sold.
That a Spain-wide distribution describes a coastal Alicante town, or that a figure labelled 'Alicante' in a press release means the province rather than the city.
That the clock the seller feels (first agent, first photograph, first viewing) is the clock any published figure starts on.
production_hook: Seven months "on the market" — but nobody measures that clock the way you think. What the published figures actually count, and what evidence would genuinely tell you something about your own street.

current_research_question: Which published institutional and commercial instruments provide housing-price information covering this market, what does each measure, and at what geography?
must_establish: Establish each producer separately and state what it measures and at what geography: MIVAU valor tasado = appraisal evidence; Notariado = notarised deed-price evidence; Registradores = registered-sale evidence; Catastro = administrative reference-value evidence; INE IPV = a price index published at Spain and autonomous-community level; private portals = advertised asking-price data. Do not force these producers into a single official/not-official count.
Establish whether any of these publishes a figure for the specific town being written about, and what coverage or population threshold decides which municipalities appear at all.

Establish the direction and magnitude of registered transaction counts for Alicante province over the most recent published periods, from the statistical office's own series, and set that beside each price series before drawing any conclusion about either.

Establish whether any source supports a causal link between asking-price level and how long a home stays listed; if none does, the piece may describe the gap between series but must not assert the cause.

Name the instrument beside every figure and keep the categories apart: MIVAU valor tasado is appraisal; the Consejo General del Notariado and the Colegio de Registradores publish completed transaction and registration evidence; private portals publish asking prices. Do not describe these as two official instruments when several institutional series exist.
never_assume: That two price series can be subtracted to yield a 'negotiation margin' or 'discount' — they are different instruments, not versions of one number.
That a figure labelled 'Alicante' is provincial; check whether the publisher means the city.
That rising prices and rising sales move together, or that a record price level is evidence that homes are selling.
That an index of percentage change can be used to state a level in euros, or that a provincial average describes a coastal resort town.

current_research_question: In a Comunitat Valenciana residential sale, which documents does the law expressly prevent a notary from authorising the deed without, which ones instead affect only the price or the buyer's mortgage, and which merely expose the seller to a penalty after the event?
must_establish: Establish, from the governing statute in each case, which requirement is an express prohibition on authorising the deed and which is not — and quote the provision rather than paraphrasing a summary site.

Establish what the property register requires before a buyer can be inscribed, and what happens where the seller's own title was never registered (an inheritance never accepted and adjudicated, a deceased co-owner still on the register, an unregistered divorce settlement).
Establish how an undeclared extension, pool or enclosed terrace is treated on a sale — whether it prevents the deed, prevents registration, or affects only valuation and the buyer's lending.

Establish the current status of the Valencian second-occupancy licence framework, of the energy certificate obligation, and of any registration number required for a property that has been let short-term — and flag, in the piece, any point that could not be confirmed from the responsible administration's own text.
never_assume: That every mandatory document is a hard stop at the notary — some are sanctions, some are price problems, and that distinction is the whole piece.
That a repaid mortgage is a cancelled charge; economic repayment and cancellation on the register are separate acts with separate costs.
That a deadline quoted for one certificate applies to another — check which statute each deadline actually comes from and what procedure it governs.

That a seller's nationality settles their tax residence, their immigration category, or which party the town hall or the Treasury will pursue; passport, residence status and tax residence are three separate things and must not be filed under one another.
production_hook: The viewings went fine. The buyer said yes. The sale died at the notary's desk. Which pieces of paper can legally stop a signing on the Costa Blanca — and which ones only cost you money.

current_research_question: What does Spanish and Valencian law actually regulate about instructing an estate agent to sell a home — commission, exclusivity, duration, the right to withdraw, the agent's own registration — and what is left entirely to whatever the seller signed?
must_establish: Establish whether estate agency commission rates, exclusivity clauses or mandate duration are regulated or capped by any Spanish statute, and what any published national commission range is and is not evidence of.

Establish the conditions under which a seller acting as a consumer has a statutory right to withdraw from a signed mandate, whether the place the contract was concluded changes the period, and what follows if the agent never disclosed that right.

Establish whether an agent operating in the Comunitat Valenciana must appear in a public register, when that obligation took effect, what the entry requires of the agent, and exactly how a seller can search it and what the search cannot do.

Establish what is and is not known about the effect of one property appearing as several separate advertisements — do not assert an effect on price or on time to sell without a source that measured it.
never_assume: That a 'standard' or 'usual' commission exists as a legal or measured fact; a published national range is neither an Alicante median nor a rule.
That VAT is included in a quoted commission, or that a quoted percentage is what lands on the invoice.
That a cooling-off right applies to every mandate — it turns on how and where the contract was concluded, and on what the agent disclosed.
That multi-agency listing, or exclusivity, has a proven effect on outcome; that is a claim requiring evidence, not a starting assumption.
production_hook: The same home can appear with several agents and several prices. Your mandate matters — but so do Spanish consumer rules and the Valencian agent regime. Here is what the contract controls and what the law controls.

current_research_question: Which published instruments can and cannot tell a Costa Blanca seller whether holding out for a better offer has paid off, and what do the most recent readings of each show for this province and — where such a series exists at all — for the specific town?
must_establish: Establish separately, and label as such, the latest asking-price, registered-sale-price and appraisal-value readings for Alicante province, and state which of the three — if any — is published for the individual town the post names, and which body publishes it.

Establish the direction and size of the change in registered transaction volume in Alicante province against the national change over the same period, taken from the statistics office's own series, and record the extraction date.

Establish what the published time-on-market figure actually measures (advert duration? whose homes? which platform?), and whether any reading exists below national or city level; treat the widely circulated "80–90 day average" as unsourced unless a primary release is located.

Establish whether any published source measures the gap between first asking price and final registered sale price at province or town level — and if none does, say so plainly instead of estimating one.
never_assume: That record prices and falling volume point the same way for one seller — they are separate measurements of separate things, and neither is a prediction.

That a province-wide figure describes a coastal town. "Alicante" is published as both a province and a municipality, by official producers and portals alike, so establish which one a figure means before using it — and check the territorial detail of the particular series rather than assuming. The ministry's appraisal series both stratifies and tabulates at municipalities of more than 25,000 inhabitants; INE's transmissions statistic (ETDP) is disseminated only by province and comunidad autónoma, with no municipal tier at all; the Notariado's own housing portal goes far below municipality, but by letting you draw the area rather than by any fixed administrative tier; and the Catastro publishes average €/m² value modules by homogeneous valuation area.

That a listing leaving a portal means a house sold — withdrawals, expiries, agent switches and re-listings all end an advert without a sale, and multi-agency listings run several clocks on one property.
That any "average days to sell" number is real; a distribution has no mean you can read off it, and figures repeated verbatim across agency websites are not a source.
production_hook: Transaction volume and price indicators can move in opposite directions. What are Alicante province's latest readings, and what does each measure?

current_research_question: In a Costa Blanca residential sale, which costs and obligations does the law allocate by default, which are purely local custom, and which does a buyer's adviser typically ask the seller to concede or have retained from the price at completion?
must_establish: Establish the Código Civil default allocation of deed-origination, first-copy and registry costs on a sale, and whether the parties may lawfully vary it by agreement — quote the operative wording.

Establish who the law names as taxpayer for the municipal land-value tax on an onerous transfer, whether that changes when the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether a clause agreed between buyer and seller binds the town hall.
Establish which certificates and documents the seller must produce for the sale, who bears the cost of each, and whether there is any the notary is legally barred from proceeding without.

Establish, and distinguish, the sums that may leave the price at completion: any statutory withholding on a non-resident's sale, and any voluntary retention a buyer's side asks for — and on what basis each is claimed.
never_assume: That local custom — "on this coast the buyer pays everything" — is the legal position; establish the statutory default and the fact that it can be varied only by agreement.
That the withholding taken from a non-resident seller's price and a retention held by the buyer's lawyer are the same money, or that either is a final tax bill rather than a payment on account.
That the same paperwork is demanded in every Alicante municipality, or that a rule described on an agency blog is still current.
That estate agency commission has a legal rate or ceiling, or that any published percentage range was measured on this coast rather than nationally.
production_hook: The price is one line of the offer. Notary costs, signing date, statutory withholdings and any additional agreed retention are separate lines — and only some are fixed by law.

current_research_question: At what point in a Spanish residential sale does each side become bound, and what determines the consequence when one of them pulls out?
must_establish: Whether the accepted offer itself contains agreement on the property and the price, and whether it expresses a present intention to bind — arts. 1450 and 1451 Código Civil make the sale binding on agreement as to thing and price, before delivery.
What a later reservation or arras document changes, and which form of arras applies — penitenciales, confirmatorias or penales.
What the parties can still do at each stage, and what each document costs the side that walks away.
never_assume: Never imply that only the later piece of paper creates the binding obligation.
Never state a single consequence of walking away without establishing which document, and which form of arras, actually governs.
production_hook: A buyer can become legally bound before the notary and before keys change hands. What matters is exactly what the parties agreed — offer, reservation, arras or sale contract — and whether that document contains the essential elements and an intention to bind.

current_research_question: Between accepted offer and signing, what can emerge from the registry, the cadastre, the community of owners or the lender's valuation that changes what a Costa Blanca buyer will pay — and which of those things can a seller establish about their own property before an offer ever arrives?
must_establish: Establish how building work carried out without registration is treated when the buyer wants to register — including whether an older completed work has a route onto the register, what evidence that route requires, and what the registrar must confirm before allowing it.

Establish why a lender's valuation can come in below an agreed price where the registered description and the built reality disagree, and what that does to a buyer's financing as distinct from what it does to the sale itself.

Establish what the community of owners must certify on a sale, what deadline the law gives for producing it, whether the notary may proceed without it, and what unpaid amounts attach to the property rather than to the previous owner.

Establish what a seller can obtain in advance about their own property — registry extract, cadastral record, community position, energy certificate, occupancy paperwork, any tourist-let registration — and what each will and will not reveal.
never_assume: That an unregistered extension blocks a sale — establish separately what it does to registration, to valuation, to the buyer's lending and to the price, because those are four different effects.
That every buyer discovery is a genuine reason to re-cut the price rather than a negotiating move — and do not assume the reverse either.

That the seven-day deadline people quote for a bank's outstanding-debt certificate applies to a sale; check which certificate that deadline actually governs and which certificate carries a real statutory clock.
That the surface areas in the registry, the cadastre and the listing agree, that built area and plot area are the same measure, or that a repaid mortgage has been removed from the register.
production_hook: The offer is accepted — then the buyer's side finds the closed terrace, the pool or the extra bedroom was never registered. Here is what that legitimately changes about the price, and what it doesn't.

current_research_question: Which documents, if any, does Spanish law actually prohibit a notary from authorising a residential sale deed without — who issues each one, on what timescale, and what happens to a completion that tries to proceed without it?
must_establish: Establish, from the governing statute's own consolidated text, which document(s) a notary is barred from authorising a sale deed without, and quote the operative wording rather than paraphrasing a law-firm blog

Establish who is legally responsible for issuing the community certificate, who must sign or countersign it, and whether the law binds the issuer to any period — and separately whether any comparable deadline exists for a lender's outstanding-debt certificate, or whether that is only practice
Establish whether the requirement can be dispensed with at completion, who alone has the power to do so, and what the person doing so takes on
Establish whether, and for how far back, the property itself carries liability for a previous owner's unpaid community charges, and how that period is counted
never_assume: That every document a buyer's lawyer requests is a legal stop — most are diligence and only a narrow set are statutory bars on authorising the deed

Never state the community certificate's deadline without quoting LPH art. 9.1.e (seven días naturales from request, issued by whoever exercises the secretary's functions with the president's visto bueno). Never assume the bank's outstanding-debt certificate is governed by the same instrument: Ley 2/1994 art. 2 sets its own seven-día-natural period, and it is the same length — the distinction is that the Ley 2/1994 clock is written for a subrogación of the loan, not for a cancellation payoff on a sale, so establish whether any statutory clock binds the lender in a sale at all.
That the seller's own written declaration of being up to date substitutes for the certificate
That the look-back period for the property's liability is a round number of years, or that it is counted from the sale date rather than in calendar years
production_hook: If your home sits in a community of owners, the notary is told not to authorise your sale without a certificate that comes from your building, not from you — and only the buyer can waive it.

current_research_question: What routes exist under Spanish law to bring completed building work that was never declared onto the property register, what does each route require, and what are the consequences at sale of leaving the work undeclared?
must_establish: Establish the routes by which completed but undeclared work can be registered, what evidence each route demands, and which authority or professional has to certify what

Establish what the registrar must check before allowing the older-works route, including whether any planning-enforcement entry blocks it and whether the classification of the land can rule it out entirely
Establish who determines that a planning-enforcement period has run, and whether that period is set nationally, regionally or by the individual town hall

Establish whether an undeclared extension prevents a notary authorising the deed at all, or whether the consequence sits with the buyer, the buyer's lender and the price — and cite the mechanism, not an anecdote
never_assume: That work appearing in the cadastre is therefore on the property register, or that the two records agreeing is the norm — they are separate systems
That age alone makes work registrable: the qualifying period varies and some land classifications are never time-barred
That an undeclared build stops the notary signing — establish what it actually stops before saying so
That a lender will finance square metres the register does not show; and if no sourceable statement of lender practice exists, say that rather than assert it

current_research_question: What forms of power of attorney can a Spanish notary act on for an owner selling from abroad, what must each one contain and pass through before it is usable in Spain, and what causes one to be rejected at the deed?
must_establish: Establish which routes exist for granting a POA outside Spain, and for each route what further formalities (legalisation, translation, and the order they must be done in) a Spanish notary requires before acting on it — distinguishing statute from professional practice and labelling which is which

Establish what a mandate must expressly empower for a disposal as opposed to mere administration, quoting the source: Código Civil art. 1713 — a mandate framed in general terms covers only acts of administration, and selling, mortgaging or any other act of riguroso dominio requires an express mandate. Do not assert that the power of attorney must name the specific property: no statute requires it. Identifying the finca by its registry details is standard drafting for a poder especial and must be labelled as practice, not law.
Establish which international or EU instruments do and do not remove legalisation requirements for notarial powers of attorney, checking the instrument's own scope rather than a summary of it

Establish whether any reliable source publishes typical durations for either route; if none does, say plainly that no timing can be published. OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — the agency's own observed durations may be added with period and sample size, but the public post must stand without them.
OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — the agency's own observed durations may be added with period and sample size, but the public post must stand without them.
never_assume: Never assume a document issued inside the EU needs no legalisation. Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 lists its scope exhaustively in Article 2(1), and its Annexes are multilingual standard forms, not a scope list, so check Article 2(1) and confirm that notarial powers of attorney fall outside it before saying anything about legalisation, and establish that the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention is the instrument that actually applies.
That a general power of administration authorises a sale
Any waiting time for a consular appointment, an apostille or a sworn translation — none is systematically published and it varies by country and by post
That a translation prepared before legalisation is accepted, or that a consulate's own public FAQ is authority on the legalisation point
production_hook: You do not have to fly to Spain to sign — but a power of attorney with the wrong wording, the wrong legalisation or the wrong translation can fail at the notary's desk, on the day there is no time left to fix it.

current_research_question: What must be completed, and in what sequence, before heirs of a Spanish property can pass title a buyer is able to register — and which of those steps carry a deadline, running from when?
must_establish: Establish the registry principle that determines whether a buyer can register a purchase from heirs, quote it, and establish whether any exception covers an ordinary open-market sale
Establish which inheritance step carries a statutory filing deadline, when the clock starts, whether an extension exists, by when it must be requested, and whether an extension is free of cost

Establish, from the regional government's own consolidated text and not from a summary, how inheritance tax in the Comunitat Valenciana currently treats heirs — whether the treatment is a reduction of the bill or an exemption from filing, which family groups it covers, and the dates any change takes effect
Establish whether the inheritance deed and the sale deed can be signed and lodged together, and what the registry requires before it will inscribe either
never_assume: That a reduction in the tax bill removes the obligation to file a return

Any relief percentage or the date it takes effect — these were amended recently, differ by family relationship, and the widely-quoted figures have been sourced from secondary commentary rather than the regional text
That heirs must wait for their own registration to complete before a buyer can sign
That inheritance tax is the only tax step — the town-hall land-value tax on the inheritance transfer is a separate liability to a separate authority
production_hook: The register still names someone who died. Here is the chain that has to close before a buyer can register anything — and which steps carry a legal deadline and which do not

current_research_question: Which of Decreto 98/2022's requirements for acting as an estate agent in the Comunitat Valenciana survive after STSJ CV 706/2024 of 13 December 2024 (rec. 22/2023, ECLI:ES:TSJCV:2024:5929, announced 17 January 2025), which annulled not whole articles but specific incisos — the professional-qualification requirement in art. 3 b in full, the territorial inciso in art. 3 a for online-only agents, the fixed aval and seguro de caución amounts in the solvency requirement, which the decree publishes as art. 3 c although the judgment's fundamento undécimo calls it 'apartado d', parts of art. 2.2, and art. 6 a, d and e — while leaving the duty to register, the solvency requirement itself and the distintivo intact? The CNMC records the judgment as firm on its case file LA/03/2022. Then: how can a homeowner verify what remains, and what does that verification fail to tell them?
must_establish: Establish from the governing Valencian instrument itself whether entry on the register is obligatory, from what date it bit, and which categories of agent fall outside its scope — including an agent trading here from an establishment in another territory.

Establish exactly how a member of the public can query the register today by running the query, not by describing it: which fields can be searched, which cannot, what a result row shows, and how a reader would find one specific agency in the output.

Establish what the regime requires by way of professional indemnity insurance or financial guarantee, whether those requirements differ by type of agent, and whether any transitional exemption still applies to agents trading before the regime began.
Establish what the rules require an agent to state in the written instruction document itself, and what an owner should therefore expect to see printed on it.
never_assume: Do not assume the register can be searched by agency name, trading name or tax number — confirm how the search actually behaves before instructing a reader to look someone up.
Do not assume registration means an agent is skilled, experienced or honest, or that non-registration proves fraud; it is a compliance threshold, not a quality rating.
Do not assume the Valencian position applies in Andalucía, Murcia or the Balearics, and do not assume a Spain-wide register exists.
Do not assume any guarantee or insurance figure is current — it is set by a decree that can be amended, so re-read the text rather than repeating a figure seen elsewhere.
production_hook: There is one number a Costa Blanca agent should be able to give you before you sign anything — and a public list you can check it against yourself.

current_research_question: What is a Spanish homeowner actually committing to when they sign an agency instruction — which terms are controlled by law, which are purely negotiable, and in what circumstances may the owner withdraw from it?
must_establish: Establish whether Spanish law regulates agency commission rates, mandate duration or exclusivity at all, and if it does not, identify which body of general law and which case law actually governs the contract.

Establish from the consumer statute itself what determines whether a right of withdrawal attaches to such a contract, how long the period runs, what lengthens it, and what extinguishes it once the agent has begun work.
Establish whether the withdrawal right depends on the seller qualifying as a consumer, and what changes when the property is owned by a company or by someone selling in the course of a business.
Establish how a post-termination commission clause is treated — whether an agent can still claim a fee on a buyer introduced during the mandate but completing after it, and on what that turns.
never_assume: Do not assume any commission percentage is standard, capped or VAT-inclusive; if a range is cited, say which organisation published it, for what geography, and whether it was measured or merely reported.
Do not assume exclusivity clauses, penalty clauses or commission tails are void — nor that they are enforceable exactly as drafted.
Do not assume every private seller is a consumer for these purposes, or that a foreign owner selling a second home is treated the same as a resident selling their home.
Do not assume the withdrawal period is a single fixed number of days; establish what varies it before naming any figure.
production_hook: Where you signed the agency contract may decide whether you can walk away from it — the kitchen table and the agency office are not the same thing in Spanish law.

current_research_question: How does instructing more than one agent actually work on the Costa Blanca — what does a buyer encounter when the same property appears repeatedly, what measured evidence exists on how it affects the outcome, and how is commission resolved when two agents claim the same introduction?
must_establish: Establish how commission entitlement is determined between competing agents under Spanish contract law and court decisions when more than one claims to have introduced the eventual buyer, and what a seller's exposure is.

Establish whether any measured Spanish evidence exists comparing sole-agency and multi-agency outcomes; if none is found, report that absence explicitly rather than importing a finding from another country's market.

Establish how the same property appears across portals when several agents list it, whether any published time-on-market measure counts adverts or properties, and what that counting decision does to any 'days to sell' figure.
Establish whether collaboration or shared-listing networks operate in Alicante province, how a fee is divided inside one, and whether a seller signing with one member is thereby reaching the others.
never_assume: Do not assume a listing disappearing from a portal means the property sold — withdrawals, expiries, agent changes and re-listings all end an advert without a sale.

Do not assume a widely quoted 'average days to sell' exists: check whether the source publishes an average at all or only a distribution, and whether the figure is for a city, a province or the whole country.
Do not assume the seller pays two commissions, and do not assume the seller can never end up facing two claims — establish which it is.
Do not assume UK or US findings on sole versus multi-agency transfer to Spain, where the market structure and the contract law differ.
production_hook: One house, five agencies, five separate adverts. Before you sign a second instruction, know what a buyer sees — and who is owed the fee when two agents claim the same buyer.

current_research_question: What can a homeowner ask an agent that separates a valuation built on evidence from one built to win the instruction, and which public instruments can be used to sanity-check a price for one specific Costa Blanca town?
must_establish: Establish which official instruments publish residential property prices covering Alicante province and its municipalities, precisely what each one measures, and at what geographic level each is published — including which coastal towns are too small to appear at municipal level.

Establish whether any published series gives figures for the specific town a piece names, or only for the province or the provincial capital, and require that the geography be stated every single time a figure is used.

Establish what a formal tasación is, who is authorised to issue one, what it is used for, and how it differs from an agent's market appraisal — including who pays and whether a seller needs one at all.

From the agency itself: obtain its own record of asking price versus completed price and its own instruction-to-deed timings, with the period and the number of sales behind them; if the agency cannot or will not supply them, do not write the piece with substitutes.
never_assume: Do not assume asking price, registered sale price and mortgage appraisal value are interchangeable or comparable to one another; name the instrument beside every figure and never subtract one from another.
Do not assume a province-wide figure describes a town, and do not assume a statistic headed 'Alicante' refers to the province — in several publications it means the city.
Do not assume an overpriced listing simply corrects later, and do not assume price reductions are recorded in any public series.
Do not assume the agency's own numbers are representative or independently verifiable — publish the sample size and the period alongside them, and describe them as the agency's own record.
production_hook: Any agent can quote you a big number to win the instruction. Ask two things: which price that number is measuring, and what their own listings actually completed at.

current_research_question: What does Spanish law actually impose on an estate-agency mandate signed by a private seller in the Comunitat Valenciana, what is left entirely to the parties, and which terms have been challenged?
must_establish: Establish the legal status of the estate-agency mandate in Spain — which statute, if any, governs it, and what body of law fills the gap when the seller signs as a private individual.

Establish which clauses routinely found in a nota de encargo (duration, automatic renewal, penalty for withdrawing, commission claimable after the mandate ends) have been ruled on by Spanish courts or consumer authorities, and on what basis.

Establish what the Comunitat Valenciana's agent register obliges an agent to state in the mandate document itself, and the exact steps a seller can take to verify an agent's entry — including the limits of the public search.
Establish whether a private seller has any right to withdraw from a signed mandate, and what the existence and length of that right depend on.
never_assume: that 'exclusiva' has a defined legal meaning, a standard duration or standard consequences — it is whatever the specific document says
that the seller signing is automatically a consumer in law; a company, or a seller acting professionally, is not
that a penalty clause or a post-termination commission clause is automatically valid, or automatically void — either conclusion requires the specific wording and the specific seller
that an office, a shopfront plaque or long local presence evidences registration, the required guarantee or professional indemnity insurance
production_hook: No Spanish statute defines an exclusive estate-agency mandate — it is an atypical contract, filled in by the Civil Code and by the courts. The rules about what has to appear on the listing page are state, not regional: the energy-efficiency rating must be included in any publication of a sale or rental, including portals, agency windows and the press (RD 390/2021, art. 17.3), and the advertisement must not mislead or stay silent on fundamental data (RD 515/1989, art. 3.1). The Comunitat Valenciana's Decreto 98/2022 is a different thing — it governs the agent's entry in the regional register and the distintivo showing the registry number, not the advertisement, and parts of it were annulled by the TSJCV in December 2024. Here is what to read before you sign.

current_research_question: How is entitlement to commission decided in Spain when more than one agency claims to have produced the buyer who eventually bought, and what in the seller's own arrangements determines whether they can be liable more than once?
must_establish: Establish what an agent must show to be owed commission under Spanish law and case law — the required link between the agent's work and the completed sale.
Establish whether commission can be owed on a buyer introduced during a mandate that has since ended, and what conditions courts have attached to such claims.
Establish how commission is set and charged in this market — whether any rate is regulated or capped, how tax is applied to it, and at what moment it becomes payable.
Establish what the seller must hold in writing for commission actually paid to count as a deductible cost of the sale, and whether that route differs for a seller taxed as a non-resident.
never_assume: any figure as 'the' Costa Blanca commission — no rate is set by law and no measured local median has been established, so a national published range must be labelled as exactly that
that a quoted percentage includes tax, or that the percentage is the whole cost
that 'no sale, no fee' means the seller can never owe anything in any circumstance
that a non-resident seller deducts selling costs through the same filing, or against the same rate, as a Spanish tax resident
production_hook: When two agencies claim the same buyer, commission turns on the causal link between each agent's work and the completed sale, together with the terms of the seller's mandate. It is not decided by one magic question.

current_research_question: When one Costa Blanca property is advertised simultaneously by several agencies, does any official or institutional source measure the effect on buyer reach or time to sale, and if not, which private portal or agency datasets are the only available evidence?
must_establish: Establish how the major Spanish portals treat several advertisements of the same property, and whether any dated, named source measures the effect of duplicate advertising on enquiries or on the completed sale.
Establish exactly what published time-on-market figures measure, which instrument produces them, at what geography, and whether anything exists below province level for this coast.
Establish which circulating 'average days to sell' figures can be traced to a named instrument and which are repeated without one.
Establish, for every price figure used, whether it is an asking price, a registered sale price or an appraisal value, and keep instruments unmixed within any single comparison.

Does any official or institutional source measure how simultaneous multi-agency advertising affects buyer reach or time to sale, and if not, which private portal or agency datasets are the only available evidence?
never_assume: any 'average days to sell' number — treat every mean as unsourced until traced to a named instrument, and note where the source publishes a distribution rather than an average
that an advertisement disappearing means the property sold — withdrawal, expiry, re-listing and a change of agent all end an ad without a sale

Never take a release label on trust: read the geography off the table itself, remembering that idealista publishes provincial as well as municipal series and that a headline naming 'Alicante' may mean either the province or the city.
that a listing view is an enquiry, or that an enquiry is a buyer
production_hook: Advertise with four agencies and a buyer can meet your house four times — four sets of photos, four descriptions, possibly four prices. Here is what that changes, and what no published Spanish source actually measures about it.

current_research_question: Does any published, named source measure sale outcomes by exclusive versus open or multi-agency mandate in Spain or Alicante province, and what can honestly be concluded if no local comparative dataset exists?
must_establish: Establish whether any dated study, registry series or portal dataset compares sale outcomes by listing type in Spain or in Alicante province, and say plainly if none is found rather than substituting a national or foreign study.
Establish, where a study from another market is the only evidence available, which market and which period it covers and why it may not transfer to this one.

OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — if sufficient agency data exists, compare this agency's own completed outcomes by mandate type, with sample size, period and metric definitions. The public post must stand without it.
Establish what the agency may publish about identifiable clients and properties before any past sale or client story is used.

OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — only if the agency supplies it: this agency's own completed-sale comparison of exclusive versus open mandates. The public post stands on whether any published evidence compares the two.
never_assume: that a study from another country, or a national average, describes this agency's own book
that achieved-price-against-asking-price is the same measure as a registered sale price series — say which one is being quoted
that a small number of past sales supports a general claim; state the count and the period alongside any percentage
that a client's story or a named property can be published without that client's agreement
production_hook: Ask three agents whether exclusive sells better and you will get three answers. Here is the evidence that could actually settle it for your house — and exactly how to ask for it.

current_research_question: How does Spanish law distinguish spending on a property that may be added to its acquisition value when the gain on sale is calculated from spending that may not, what documentary evidence is required for it to be accepted, and does the answer work the same way for a seller who is tax-resident in Spain and one who is not?
must_establish: Establish, from AEAT's own material and the IRPF/IRNR rules it cites, what qualifies as 'inversiones y mejoras' addable to acquisition value, and whether any category of spending is expressly excluded — do not infer the boundary from a builder's or blog's description of it.

Establish what evidence is actually required for such spending to be accepted, and report honestly if the law prescribes no fixed form: LGT art. 106.1 applies the ordinary Civil Code and LEC rules of proof, and art. 106.4 makes the invoice the priority means of justifying such expenses while stating expressly that it is not a privileged means of proof — once the Treasury founds a challenge, the taxpayer must prove the work was real. Cover what an invoice should show, why payment traceability and a contemporaneous paper trail matter in practice, and why undocumented or cash-paid work usually fails — for want of provable reality, date and amount, not by a specific statutory ban.

Establish separately how a seller's own selling costs (agency commission, certificates, notary share, plusvalía) are treated in the calculation, and confirm whether that is the same mechanism as improvements or a different one.

Establish whether the position differs for a seller filing under IRPF and one filing Modelo 210 as a non-resident, and what happens where the work was carried out by a previous owner or before an inheritance.
never_assume: Do not assume that any builder's bill reduces the tax. Where the line falls between work that counts and work that does not is the entire subject of the piece and must come from a cited source, not from the writer's expectation.

Do not assume the seller's tax rate. Residents and non-residents are taxed on a property gain under different scales, so the same deduction is worth different amounts to different owners — never blend the two into one number.
Do not assume a foreign owner is a non-resident. Tax residence turns on where the person actually lives, not on the passport, and nationality does not decide it.
Do not assume works done before the current owner acquired the property, or before an inheritance was accepted, are available to the seller now.
production_hook: Spanish tax law lets you add the cost of "investments and improvements" to what you originally paid for the place. So before you spend, say, €12,000 on that bathroom, find out what counts as one — and what paperwork has to exist for it to count.

current_research_question: When a Costa Blanca property's built reality differs from its registered and cadastral description, what routes exist to regularise it before a sale, what does each route require and cost, and what actually happens at the notary, at the registry and with a buyer's lender if the owner does nothing?
must_establish: Establish how an owner checks the discrepancy themselves: which documents (nota simple, escritura, cadastral certificate, municipal planning file) record what, how each is obtained from abroad, and what a mismatch between two of them means.

Establish the conditions, evidence and steps required for registering a completed work by antiquity under art. 28.4 TRLSRU, including what the registrar must verify beforehand and which land situations are excluded from that route.

Establish whether an unregistered extension prevents the deed being signed at all, or only affects registration, lending and price — and cite whichever turns out to be the case rather than asserting either.

Establish whether any published, sourced evidence exists for Alicante province on how unregistered surface area affects a mortgage valuation or an achieved sale price; if none exists, the piece must say so.
never_assume: Do not assume the planning-enforcement limitation period has run. It varies by autonomous community and by land classification, and in some categories it does not run at all — this must be checked, never presumed for 'old' work.
Do not conflate built area, usable area and plot area, and do not assume the cadastral surface and the registry surface are meant to be identical.
Do not treat an undeclared extension as automatically legalisable, nor as automatically illegal. Both framings are wrong and both are common.
Do not assume every buyer behaves the same. A buyer needing a Spanish mortgage and a cash buyer are not in the same position, and the piece must not merge them.
production_hook: The pool, the glazed-in terrace, the extra bedroom that used to be a naya. They are on your property — but they may not be on your deeds. Here is how to find out what your paperwork actually says, and what Spanish law offers when the building and the register disagree.

current_research_question: Which documents must a residential seller in the Comunitat Valenciana hold before listing, before signing, and at completion; who issues each one, how long does each take and what does it cost; which of them expire; and which of them a buyer can waive?
must_establish: Establish, from RD 390/2021 and from the Generalitat's own instrument, the difference between an energy certificate issued by a technician and one lodged with the regional register, which of the two has legal effect, and precisely what must appear in a public listing.

Establish the current Comunitat Valenciana position on the second-occupancy declaración responsable. The operative instrument is still Decreto 12/2021, de 22 de enero, del Consell — it was NOT touched by the 2025 legislative change. What Ley 5/2025 (DD única, g) repealed was Decreto 80/2023 on design and quality of dwellings, which is a different subject; the Generalitat's own page confirms Decreto 12/2021 remains in force and is under review, and that the Orden of 7 December 2009 on design and quality revives in Decreto 80/2023's place. Separately confirm, from the Generalitat's own text, whether the declaración responsable is required at the deed rather than relying on law-firm summaries.

Establish the community-debt certificate procedure under art. 9.1.e LPH: who issues it, the statutory deadline for issuing it, whether the buyer may expressly waive it, and what liability attaches to the property for a previous owner's unpaid charges.

Establish what a seller should ask their community of owners about works already approved but not yet billed, and how liability for those is allocated between an outgoing and incoming owner — cite the rule, do not reason it out.
never_assume: Do not assume a certificate a technician has produced is valid. Registration with the regional body is a separate step with its own deadline, and the piece must verify which state a document is in.
Do not assume validity periods are uniform across ratings or documents. Where a period is shorter for poorer-performing properties, that must be checked and stated, not averaged away.

Do not carry a deadline from one document to another. Several seven-day and one-month rules exist in this area, they belong to different statutes, and they are routinely swapped in circulating content.
Do not assume practice is uniform across Alicante province. Where a requirement at the deed depends on the town hall, say that it is municipal and name the check the owner has to make.
production_hook: If your home sits in a comunidad de propietarios, the notary cannot authorise the deed without a certificate of what you owe the community — unless your buyer expressly exonerates you (art. 9.1.e LPH), and you cannot count on that.

current_research_question: Across this agency's own completed sales, what pre-listing preparation was carried out, what did it cost the owner, and what happened to the asking price, the registered sale price and the time from listing to deed, compared with otherwise similar properties that were listed exactly as they stood?
must_establish: Establish whether any published, primary-sourced study measures the effect of specific pre-sale works on achieved sale price or time to sell in Alicante province. If none exists, the piece must state that plainly rather than importing a national, foreign or portal-blog figure.

Pull the agency's own completed sales: what preparation was done, what the owner spent, list price, registered deed price, listing date and deed date — and count the sample so the number of sales appears in the piece.

Establish the current direction of the local market from a named instrument — transaction counts and registered sale prices for Alicante province — so the agency's own results are read against the right conditions.
Establish, for every number that reaches the page, which metric it is: asking price, registered sale price, appraisal value, or days an advertisement was live.
never_assume: Do not assume a portal's days-on-market figure measures how long a property took to sell. It measures how long an advert was live, adverts end for reasons other than a sale, and one property can run several adverts at once.

Do not turn a published distribution into an average, and do not repeat any circulating 'average days to sell' figure without locating its primary source — widely repeated versions of this number have no source behind them.
Do not present a province-wide figure as a fact about a town, or a figure for the city of Alicante as a fact about the province. Portal releases routinely mean the city when they say 'Alicante'.
Do not let a handful of the agency's own sales become a market rule. State how many sales the claim rests on, in the piece, next to the claim.

current_research_question: For a residential sale in Alicante province completing in 2026, what sits between the agreed price and the seller's net receipt: which amounts are deducted or withheld at or around completion, which are a final cost, which are a payment on account that is later settled or refunded — and what, if anything, differs for a seller who is tax-resident in Spain versus one who is not?
must_establish: Establish from Agencia Tributaria's own pages how a property gain is computed, and which rate regime applies to a seller taxed as a resident versus one taxed under IRNR — including whether the rate turns on the seller's passport, their EU/EEA status, or where they are tax resident. Settled at source: a non-resident's gain on the sale of Spanish property is taxed at a flat 19% under art. 25.1.f.3º TRLIRNR, whatever the seller's nationality and whether or not they are resident in the EU/EEA. The 24%/19% split in art. 25.1.a is a different rule and applies to imputed and rental income, not to the gain. Resolve that against the primary text before any rate is written; if it cannot be resolved, the piece must not carry a rate at all.
Establish which of the seller's selling costs reduce the taxable transmission value and which do not.

Establish who is legally liable for plusvalía municipal on a sale, whether that liability sits differently where the seller is a non-resident individual, and whether the amount is set municipality by municipality — so whether any province-wide figure can exist.

Establish the mechanism by which a percentage of the price is retained from a non-resident seller: who pays it to whom, on what form, and by what route the seller recovers any excess. Confirm both filing deadlines against a primary source — they currently rest on secondary sources only.

Do not import an IRPF habitual-residence exemption into IRNR by analogy. Establish each relief separately from current AEAT and TRLIRNR authority for this seller. The non-resident reinvestment relief has its own statutory conditions for qualifying EU/EEA residents; any over-65 relief for a non-resident must be independently established from current primary authority before it is mentioned.
never_assume: Never let nationality decide the tax. Establish the seller's tax residence under the applicable statutory criteria and, where relevant, the tax treaty. Tax residence is a legal status; it must not be reduced to nationality, immigration status or ordinary-language 'where the person lives'.

Never publish an agency commission percentage as typical or standard: no rate is regulated in Spain and no verified Costa-Blanca-measured median exists. If commission appears at all, it is the rate in that agency's own mandate. Agency services do carry VAT, but never state whether a quoted percentage is VAT-inclusive or VAT-exclusive — that is a fact of the individual mandate. Say it must be checked; do not supply a default either way.

Establish separately, from the primary text, who each relief reaches: the reinvestment exemption is extended to non-residents of the EU/EEA with effective exchange of information by DA 7ª TRLIRNR. For any over-65 relief, identify the actual authority that applies it to a non-resident before mentioning it at all, rather than describing how it has been interpreted. Establish the property's status and the seller's tax residence first.
Never state the current rate scale from memory: the top savings-base bracket changed with effect from 2025, and rates must be read from the amended article, not recalled.
production_hook: The price you agree is not the money that reaches your account. Here is what sits in between — which amounts are a final cost, which are payments on account settled later, and what changes if you are not tax-resident in Spain.

current_research_question: In a Comunitat Valenciana residential sale, which documents and registry facts must be in place before a notary can authorise the deed — and which widely repeated 'requirements' in fact expose the seller only to a cost, a sanction, or a lower price, without blocking the signing?
must_establish: Establish, from the governing statute rather than commentary, which document a notary is expressly prohibited from authorising a deed without: who issues it, on what deadline, and whether any party is able to waive it — and if so, at what risk to whom.

Establish what the registry requires as to who is shown as owner, and what happens when the person selling is not the registered owner — an inheritance never inscribed, a divorce settlement never registered, a deceased co-owner never removed.
Do not state that absence of the energy certificate or Valencian occupancy paperwork prevents notarial authorisation unless current primary authority expressly establishes that consequence.

Establish how an undeclared extension, pool or enclosed terrace is treated: whether a regularisation route exists, what conditions it carries, and what the works actually affect — registrable title, a lender's valuation, the achievable price — rather than whether they 'stop the sale'.
never_assume: Never carry a deadline across regimes. A seven-day issuing deadline that is real for one certificate does not exist for the bank's outstanding-debt certificate on a sale — that specific error is already circulating widely.
Do not state that absence of the energy certificate or Valencian occupancy paperwork prevents notarial authorisation unless current primary authority expressly establishes that consequence.

Never assume the Valencian second-occupancy paperwork is what an older article says it is, and never present one town hall's practice at the deed as the regional rule. Check the Generalitat's own instrument.

Never present a national default as what will apply — the Código Civil's default allocation of notary costs is expressly overridable, and local Costa Blanca practice commonly overrides it. What governs is the contract.
production_hook: Buyer found, price agreed — and the community-debt certificate has an express statutory no-authorisation rule unless the buyer waives it. Other documents and title facts have different legal effects and must be checked separately. Here is what genuinely blocks, delays or merely costs money at completion.

current_research_question: For heirs of a property in Alicante province, what has to be completed, and in what order, between a death and a buyer being able to register their purchase; which of those steps run to a deadline; and what does missing one actually cost?
must_establish: Establish the sequence from death certificate through to the buyer's registration of title, and establish specifically whether the inheritance deed and the sale deed can be signed and lodged together or must be separated — and what a buyer's registration depends on.

Establish the filing deadline for the inheritance tax, whether an extension exists, by when it must be requested, whether silence grants it, and whether it carries a cost — read from the regulation itself.

Establish the current Comunitat Valenciana inheritance-tax relief position by kinship group, from the Generalitat's own consolidated text. The percentages and the dates on which one group's relief steps up are at present secondary-sourced only, and one of those steps falls inside 2026 — the piece must not carry a number that has not been read at source.
Establish whether the relief removes the obligation to file, or only reduces what is payable, and whether it applies to assets that were not declared.
never_assume: Never call the Valencian relief an exemption, and never apply it to every heir — it is set by kinship group and the groups are treated differently. A child is not a niece.
Never assume 'nothing to pay' means 'nothing to file' or 'nothing to register'. Establish each separately.

Never carry the tax treatment of inheriting into the tax treatment of selling. The later sale is its own taxable event, governed by the seller's own tax residence — not the deceased's, and not the heir's nationality.

Never assume heirs living abroad are in the same position as heirs living in Spain. But do not carry the EEA/non-EEA split into the inheritance tax itself: since Ley 11/2021 (in force 11 July 2021) amended DA 2ª of Ley 29/1987, non-resident heirs are entitled to the autonomous community's own rules regardless of whether they live in the EU, the EEA or a third country. The EEA line does still bite at the later SALE — the reinvestment exemption in DA 7ª TRLIRNR reaches EU and EEA residents only — so keep the two stages apart. Establish each.
production_hook: You inherited a place on the Costa Blanca and now want to sell it. One of the clocks started on the day of the death — not the day you decided.

current_research_question: What public evidence exists on the duration of each stage of a Costa Blanca sale, what exactly does each source time, and where does no public duration series exist?
must_establish: For every metric researched — for example median days on market, discount to asking price or price per m² — name the metric explicitly, then establish whether a published series exists for Alicante province or the named town.

Establish whether a quoted 'average days to sell' traces to a named instrument and a publisher's own release. A cluster of near-identical figures circulating verbatim across agency sites has already been found to misstate the source it cites — trace every number, or drop it.

Establish which steps between offer and signing have a stateable legal or administrative duration (a tenant's pre-emption notice period, a certificate issuer's statutory deadline, an inheritance step) and which have no published duration whatsoever, including any route requiring a power of attorney granted outside Spain.

Establish the agency's own record: how many sales it completed in a stated period, and the actual span for each, with the two dates defined explicitly (mandate signed to deed signed, or offer accepted to deed signed — chosen once and stated).
OPTIONAL AGENCY ADDENDUM — only if the agency supplies it: their own completed-sale timelines, with the sale count and period stated. The post must stand up without it.
never_assume: Never convert a distribution into an average. A published breakdown of how many sales fell into each time band does not yield a mean, and any 'average' derived from one is invented.

Never treat a listing coming down as a sale. Ads end through withdrawal, expiry, switching agent and re-listing — and multi-agency listing, common here, runs several independent clocks on one property.

Never let a figure for the city of Alicante stand in for the province or for a coastal town. In portal releases 'Alicante' usually means the city, which is not a resort market — say which geography every number belongs to.
Never publish a waiting time for a consular appointment, an apostille, or a sworn translation. No source establishes a typical duration, and it varies by country and post.

current_research_question: Which instrument publishes the nationality of home buyers in Alicante province — noting that the REGISTRY series (Colegio de Registradores' Estadística Registral Inmobiliaria) publishes nationality only nationally and by autonomous community, and gives the province just the foreigners' share, so province-level nationality comes from the NOTARIAL series (Consejo General del Notariado, published for Alicante by the Colegio Notarial de Valencia), which counts deeds rather than registrations. What exactly does it count (transactions or value; province or municipality; latest reference period), and what does a recorded nationality establish and fail to establish about that buyer's tax residence, immigration category and financing?
must_establish: Identify the primary instrument that publishes buyer nationality for Spanish property purchases; record its exact geography (province vs municipality), its metric (count of transactions vs value), its publisher and its latest reference period, and record whether any Alicante town-level breakdown exists at all.
Establish whether that series separates foreign nationals resident in Spain from those resident abroad, and state which of the two the headline figure is.

Establish from primary immigration and tax sources the boundaries a nationality alone cannot settle: which nationalities are EEA and therefore outside the 90/180 third-country clock, where Switzerland sits, and on what basis Spanish tax residence is determined.
Establish whether the nationality ranking moved between the two most recent published periods, and by how much, before any trend is described.
never_assume: that the leading foreign nationality province-wide is the leading nationality in any particular town
that the post-Brexit position of a British buyer describes a Norwegian, Icelandic, Liechtenstein or Swiss buyer
that 'foreign buyer' implies non-resident, cash-funded, or buying a second home
that share of transactions equals share of money spent
production_hook: A foreign passport does not tell you whether your buyer lives here, pays tax here, or needs a mortgage — here is what the purchase records actually record about who buys on this coast

current_research_question: For Alicante province, compare each series separately: Consejo General del Notariado notarised deed prices and transactions; Colegio de Registradores registered transaction and price series; MIVAU valor tasado appraisal values; INE transfer counts where applicable; and private portal asking prices. State the publisher, the event measured, the geography and the reference period beside every figure.
must_establish: Pull the transaction-count series for Alicante province from the primary statistics source for the latest published month; record the extraction date and whether the figures are provisional and subject to revision.

Record separately, for each price instrument, its geography, metric, reference period and publisher; establish whether a province-level asking-price figure exists on a primary page rather than in a press summary, and do not carry forward any figure that cannot be traced to one.
Establish whether new-build and second-hand counts moved in the same direction in the same period, and report them separately.
Establish whether transaction counts and price series have diverged before in this province's own published history, without asserting a cause for it.
never_assume: that a movement in the average price of homes sold means individual homes changed in value
that the three price instruments are versions of one number, or that they can be compared or subtracted from one another
that a province-wide count describes the seller's own town, property type or price band
that a falling transaction count means homes are not selling — establish what the count is a count of
production_hook: Transaction counts and price indicators can move in opposite directions in the same province. Before you set an asking price, look up Alicante's latest readings — and know what each of those numbers is actually counting.

current_research_question: Which Alicante-province municipalities have price or transaction figures published by an official statistical instrument, what is the publication threshold and where is it stated, and what evidence about local demand exists for the towns that fall below it?
must_establish: Establish what geographic resolution each source actually reaches: the ministry's municipal series, the registrars' series, and the Portal Estadístico del Notariado, which publishes average price per m2, average total price and transaction counts down to postcode and custom-drawn areas — so a sub-municipal locality like Moraira may be invisible to one source and visible to another.

Confirm from the ministry's own published tables, not from a secondary report, the rule governing which municipalities get disaggregated price data, and list which Alicante coastal municipalities meet it in the latest published quarter.
Establish whether any other official body publishes municipal-level transaction counts or buyer profiles for Alicante province, and at what geography and metric.
Establish what portals or private indices publish at town level, and record explicitly for each whether it measures asking price, registered sale price, or listing counts.
never_assume: that a provincial or coastal-strip average describes an individual town or urbanisation
that a portal's town page is reporting sale prices
that a neighbouring town's published figure can substitute for an unpublished one
that an agency's own enquiry count is a measure of the whole town's market
production_hook: Moraira is part of the municipality of Teulada, so municipality-only statistics cannot isolate Moraira as a separate municipality. The Notariado portal can go finer, including postcode and custom-drawn areas.

current_research_question: In Alicante province, how have new-build and second-hand transaction counts (INE ETDP / MIVAU) and the registrars' registered sale price index (Colegio de Registradores, ERI) moved relative to each other across the latest published periods — noting that the counts and the price come from different publishers on different calendars — and what does that split establish, and not establish, about the buyers a resale seller is competing for?
must_establish: Separate the new-build and second-hand transaction series for Alicante province from the primary statistics source for the latest published periods, recording reference months and provisional status.
Establish how the statistics define a new-build transmission, how long after completion a home stops being counted as new, and whether a fully renovated resale is classified as either.
Establish whether registered sale price and appraisal value are published separately for new and used homes at province level, and on what dates.

Establish what is published about new-build supply in the province and name precisely which measure it is — planning permits, starts, or completions — rather than describing it generically as 'supply'.
never_assume: that new-build and resale buyers are the same pool, or separate pools, without evidence
that an average new-build price premium is a premium available on any individual property
that permits, starts and completions are interchangeable measures of supply
that province-wide new-build activity is spread evenly across the coastal towns
production_hook: Your competition is not only other resales — the buyer viewing your house is weighing up new builds too. Here is what the registered sales say about how the two are actually moving in this province.
